edits.old: Restrict database traffic to trusted clients using private networks and firewall or security-group rules; enabling authentication does not replace network restrictions. (high confidence)
edits.new: Restrict database traffic to trusted clients using a trusted/private network and firewall or security-group rules. MongoDB lists enabling authentication and hardening network infrastructure as separate, complementary measures. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-hardening.md

evidence.quote: Ensure that MongoDB runs in a trusted network environment and configure firewall or security groups to control inbound and outbound traffic for your MongoDB instances.
Allow only trusted clients to access the network interfaces and ports on which MongoDB instances are available.
If your system has more than one network interface, bind MongoDB programs to the private or internal network interface.
At minimum, consider [enabling authentication](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md#std-label-checklist-auth) and [hardening network infrastructure.]

statements.statement: Restrict database traffic to trusted clients using firewall or security-group rules.

statements.note: Trusted network environment, and bind to the private/internal interface.

statements.statement: Enabling authentication does not replace network restrictions.
statements.note: Not stated explicitly; the docs list authentication and network hardening as separate minimum measures.

edits.rationale: The checklist supports trusted networks, firewall/security-group rules and trusted-client-only access. The hardening page lists authentication and network hardening as separate minimum steps and recommends binding to the private interface. No source states in so many words that authentication does not replace network restrictions, so that phrasing is dropped.

edits.old: Review security logs and privileges regularly, and keep MongoDB and its host patched; these are ongoing operational controls. (high confidence)
edits.new: Collect logs to a central log store, review MongoDB database users and periodically rotate them, and periodically apply patches to the host and upgrade MongoDB; the checklist groups these under periodic/ongoing production checks. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md

evidence.quote: Periodically check for [MongoDB Product CVE](https://www.mongodb.com/alerts) and upgrade your products .
Periodically apply patches to your machine.
Review MongoDB database users and periodically rotate them.
Collect logs to a central log store. These logs contain database authentication attempts including source IP addresses.

statements.note: Checklist says to collect logs centrally, not to review them regularly.
Checklist says to review database users and rotate them, not privileges.

statements.statement: Keep MongoDB and its host patched.
statements.note: Upgrade products and apply patches periodically.

edits.rationale: The checklist's ongoing checks cover patching the machine, upgrading MongoDB, and reviewing and rotating database users. It advises central log collection but does not say to regularly review security logs or privileges.

edits.old: MongoDB binaries bind to localhost by default. Flare explains that a container binding to all interfaces becomes externally reachable only when networking and port publication expose it; internet exposure must be assessed from the deployment configuration. (high confidence)
edits.new: Self-managed MongoDB binaries (mongod and mongos) bind to localhost by default. Flare reports that images with a configuration binding MongoDB to all network interfaces can become internet-accessible when deployed with public port mappings or host networking; exposure should be assessed from the deployment configuration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-hardening.md ; https://www.esecurityplanet.com/threats/mongodb-ransomware-is-still-actively-hitting-exposed-databases/

edits.old: MongoDB security operations guidance includes reviewing product CVEs, applying upgrades, reviewing network-rule changes, and auditing user privileges; hardening is an ongoing process. (high confidence)
edits.new: MongoDB's security checklist lists periodic/ongoing production checks: check product CVEs and upgrade, review policy and procedure changes (especially network rules, to prevent inadvertent internet exposure), apply patches, and review MongoDB database users and periodically rotate them. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md

evidence.quote: Periodically check for [MongoDB Product CVE](https://www.mongodb.com/alerts) and upgrade your products .
Review policy/procedure changes, especially changes to your network rules to prevent inadvertent MongoDB exposure to the Internet.
Review MongoDB database users and periodically rotate them.

statements.statement: Guidance includes reviewing product CVEs and applying upgrades.

statements.note: Checklist says review database users and rotate them.
Supported only by the 'Periodic/Ongoing Production Checks' section.

edits.rationale: The checklist has a 'Periodic/Ongoing Production Checks' section covering CVEs, upgrades, network-rule changes and database user review and rotation. It does not mention auditing user privileges, and it does not say in prose that hardening is an ongoing process beyond that section.

edits.old: TLS protects client and cluster communication; storage encryption and application-side field encryption address different data exposure boundaries. Security articles should explain these controls separately. (high confidence)
edits.new: TLS/SSL encrypts communication between clients and MongoDB and between cluster components such as mongod and mongos; storage-layer encryption (WiredTiger Encryption at Rest) and application-side field encryption (Queryable Encryption or Client-Side Field Level Encryption) are separate controls that protect data at different points. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-encryption-at-rest.md
